| [CLAIM-268](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-268.md) | Model stitching certifies an order of information only in its reconstruction form: a map fitted to reproduce the target layers shows the source representation is at least as informative for every decision on the label, task-loss stitching compares one decision problem through a fixed head, and a failure to stitch is no evidence against sufficiency | The general content of [CLAIM-126](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-126.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the result about stitching does not rest on [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s account of fidelity. Reconstruction-fitted stitching makes the target a garbling of the source given the label, which certifies one direction of Blackwell sufficiency ([THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md)). Task-loss stitching ([LIT-850](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-850.md)) compares one decision problem through a fixed head, orders neither representation, and is not invariant under reparametrisation. In both forms a failure says only that no map in the class works. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md) | A regularized linear readout can tell apart only representations that differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed, so any distinction beyond that is supplied by the analyst, not by the readouts | The general content of [CLAIM-193](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the linear result does not rest on [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), whose realist reading is about communicative identity. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). Kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed ([THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md)). An inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)). And spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). These are proved results for learned representations. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-270](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-270.md) | Retaining information about where a Markov chain started and staying close to the starting distribution are different properties: a chain can forget its initial state while its distribution stays far from where it began, so convergence is not preservation and losing information about the origin is not degradation | The general content of [CLAIM-081](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the distinction does not rest, through [CLAIM-056](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-056.md), on [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s account of fidelity. I(U_0; U_n) and D[P(U_n), P(U_0)] answer different questions. A contractive chain loses information about its initial state while converging to a stationary distribution that can be far from the start. The data-processing inequality bounds the first and says nothing about the second. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-271](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-271.md) | A collective's reasons need not be any of its members' reasons, so aggregating members' conclusions, as polling does, can yield verdicts the collective's own reasons do not support | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-13, given in conversation by refining "the good of a higher level agent need not align with the respective goods of the parts" to reasons. The assistant drew the polling consequence. On [THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md) a group that judges linked propositions must choose between aggregating premises and aggregating conclusions, and the two can disagree. A poll aggregates conclusions. It does not say that polling is illegitimate, nor that the collective knows better than its members. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-272](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-272.md) | Giving every member an equal budget of actions does not equalize their influence, because coordination lets a member's plan direct other members' actions, so a cap on self-allocation constrains action and not authority | A8 §3 on the owner's r/place case. Every account had the same cooldown, a ban on self-allocation at the level of pixels, yet "a participant who creates a successful design template might have almost no direct pixel- writing capacity beyond any ordinary user, yet exercise enormous influence". A8: "Reddit's software imposed a cooldown and common action budget, but did not give participants equal *effective* influence." It qualifies [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md): the budget constrains moves, and endorsement moves authority. It does not say the inequality is illegitimate. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-273](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-273.md) v2 | A maintained r/place artwork is a dissipative structure in Prigogine's structural sense, order held only by a sustained flow of repair against rival coalitions and against unaffiliated placement whose rate falls over the event, but its order is imported from a design and not born of an instability | The owner, on reading Wu and Silva's finding that lasting artworks are those whose coalitions keep working under continual overwriting: "sounds like there's likely a connection to dissipative structure here". It holds for half of Prigogine's criterion ([NOTE-424](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-424.md)): an open system kept from the state it would drift to by a sustained flow, here of placements. The flow works against two sources of corruption. One is rival coalitions. The other is unaffiliated placement, a real decay whose rate falls over the event (version 2, the owner's correction, [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md)). It fails for the other half, since an artwork's order comes from a template, not from an instability (Adams et al.). No thermodynamic quantity is defined. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md) | Participation on a shared canvas thins selectively: people keep coming back while art they invested in survives, so unaffiliated corruption falls over the event and the remaining participants are weighted toward maintainers, a cooling schedule the population produces for itself | The owner's correction to [CLAIM-273](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-273.md). Over days, random participation is a real decay, and it is not constant. Uninvested participants drop out, and invested ones stay while their art persists, which "creat[es] a survival function that biases towards user's sustaining participation if the art they are invested in persists". So the "temperature" of random corruption is high early and low late. This is a feedback from pattern to flow, and it answers [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) in part. Untested on the logs. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-275](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-275.md) | An intervention can come before the interpretation it makes available, so in an organization of processes meaning, policy and influence co-evolve and none of them is simply upstream of the others | A4 §6, on the record's two accounts of emotion, Frijda's appraisal upstream of action readiness and Barrett's construction, and the owner's two replies at U5: "yes, exactly" to "meaning, policy, and influence can co-evolve", and "so much yes" to "An operator may act not because it already possesses an interpretation, but because its intervention creates the conditions under which a particular interpretation becomes available." The first filing left both out. It does not say interpretation never comes first. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-276](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-276.md) | A shared interpretation's coherence, its fidelity to evidence and the plurality of live alternatives are separate quantities, and a population can raise the first while lowering the other two, so a collective interpretation's stability is no evidence of its truth | A1 §6, before the influence canvas: meaning as "metastable patterns of mutually reinforcing constraints", with the caveat that "delusions, dogmas, and self-reinforcing errors can also become metastable". So coherence C(M), evidential fidelity F(M, Y) and plurality P(M) must be measured apart. Zollman's result that sparser communication helps a community settle on the better option ([THEORY-143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-143.md)) and Holman and Bruner's industrial selection ([THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md)) are the record's readings that bear on it. It does not say coherence is bad. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md) | Durable authority among an organization's processes need not be a primitive: trust can be the temporal regularity of endorsement that policies earn by being right often, and the same loop entrenches whatever gained influence early | The owner's objection at U5 to A4's call to keep "persistent authority structures" distinct from "transient endorsement updates": "I'd expect persistent authority to be an emergent property here as 'right a lot' policies become distinguished into 'trusted' policies." A5 granted it. Momentary endorsement, established trust and institutionalized authority are regimes of one process, set by how slowly endorsers forget. A5 added the converse: the same loop turns an early lead into durable authority. The claim does not say which of the two a given organization does. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) | An operator framework flexible enough to redescribe any dynamical process explains none of them until it forbids some outcome, and the shared-organization thesis has not yet said what it forbids | A7 §14's own first limitation, which the exchange granted and the record files as the standing objection to the explanatory thesis: "A sufficiently flexible operator framework could redescribe almost any dynamical process. The model must earn its value through restrictive assumptions, predictive compression, and intervention-sensitive predictions." It is [CLAIM-024](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-024.md)'s objection to the will paper, met by a second account. It is answered by a prediction the framework makes and its rivals do not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-279](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-279.md) | Whether an intervention stabilizes or destabilizes a pattern is relative to a policy and a frame, so denoiser, critic and re-noiser are regimes an operator falls into, not kinds of operator | The owner at U3 proposed operators that may "*re*noise the region it has influence over e.g. because it disagrees with the direction of the current work", and at U5 that named operator types are "just different regimes in the dynamics of our general process", with niches emerging. A5 granted it. A8 grounded it in the owner's r/place case: restoring a pixel is denoising for the group whose image it is and destruction for the group overwriting it. The claim does not say specialization always emerges. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) | A pattern can persist while every constituent is replaced and some constituents work against it, as a high-turnover regime of damage and repair, so the persistence of a product and the persistence of the organization producing it are separate facts | A8 §4 and §9, on the owner's r/place case. An artwork defended for days has its pixels repeatedly replaced, its defenders come and go, and its attackers keep working, yet the image stays recognizable. Its stability is continuous activity, not the absence of it. A8: "the distinction between a persistent product and a persistent producer". An image can outlast the coalition behind it, and a coalition can outlast the images it makes. The claim does not say that the pattern, or the coalition, is a self. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-281](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-281.md) | Endorsement indexed by role lets a process empower another as a critic while opposing its preferred policy, so an organization that allocates authority by role can keep disagreement working inside it instead of sorting into factions | A2 §8, on the owner's U2 design. If processes endorse only those whose policies match their own, the influence structure "risks degenerating into factions of mutually reinforcing beliefs". Indexing endorsement by role, E_i(j, r, c, t), lets i back j as an error detector without backing j's authority over the final choice. [CASE-080](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-080.md) is the worked example. It does not say role boundaries hold under pressure. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) | The precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it are different quantities, and internal conflict is the gap between them | A4 §2, reading Frijda through the record: "control precedence also suggests a useful addition to our parameterization", a priority p_i claimed by a process, which "is not the same as granted influence I_i. An operator can urgently demand control without receiving it. That distinction between *claimed precedence* and *endorsed authority* may be essential to modeling internal conflict." It joins [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) to the endorsement scheme. It does not say which wins. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) | A self, in the self-governing sense, is a historically continuous organization of processes that takes part in governing the conditions of its own persistence, differentiation and transformation, not merely one that persists | A10 §11's central hypothesis, reached after the owner asked at U10 for a research programme on a constitutive theory of selfhood. It treats the endogeneity of governance as the distinguishing mark: the processes do not only run inside an architecture, they change which processes can act and how the organization will operate. A11 named its falsifier. "Self" is in [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s self-governing sense, with persisting and integrated senses nearby, and not the subject sense. Proposed, and under the record's objections: [CLAIM-116](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-116.md), [CLAIM-165](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-165.md), [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md) and the counter filed with it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) | An endorsement scheme can deny each operator control over its own authority and still reward it for delegating, because the authority an operator holds and how far its preferred policies are realized are different quantities | The owner's design at U2 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: operators vote on one another's influence, cannot significantly manipulate their own, and gain by finding aligned operators and delegating authority to them. A2 made it precise. Two conditions are imposed: each operator's own authority is insensitive to its own endorsements, and its payoff is how closely the collective decision matches what it would endorse. Under them, empowering a better-placed ally is a way to get one's policies realized without becoming more powerful. It does not say such schemes resist collusion, or that alignment makes delegation wise. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-286](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-286.md) | Habit, akrasia, rumination, rigidity and insight can be modelled as regimes of one organization, in which processes transform shared meaning and allocate one another's influence, with trust, specialization and higher-level agency arising from its history and not imposed | A7's central thesis, the explanatory half of the manuscript, kept apart from the constitutive half ([CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md)) as A7 itself asked. Its novelty is the unification, not any ingredient: "multi-agent cognition, competing control systems, temporal discounting, self-exciting processes, and organizational emergence all have substantial literatures". It is the claim [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) objects to. It does not say these processes are a self. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) | What persists when a self persists through inactivity is the capacity to reinstate an organization, not its continuous running, and continuity of that kind can branch and merge, so it is not an identity relation | A6 §7 and A10 §4.3. A6 separated activation continuity, organizational continuity and policy continuity, and put identity in the second: "A dormant coalition can remain available for reactivation because learned parameters, memory traces, and endorsement structures persist." A10 added that continuity of descent "is not automatically an equivalence relation. Organizational histories can branch, merge, and partially overlap." It sits beside [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md), which asks for a coherence measure conserved along a system's own trajectory, and qualifies it for gaps. It uses [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s persisting sense. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) | A simulation whose operators each maximize an objective the modeller fixed cannot show self-constitution, because the norms the organization appears to maintain are then the modeller's, not set by the organization itself | The record's objection, raised by no one in the exchange. A2 gives each operator an objective J_i, its evaluation of the collective decision, and A7 and A10 propose sufficiency tests run on such populations. Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde hold that systems optimizing an externally fixed function are not models of agency ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md), C5), and Di Paolo (2005) that a system's norms must be norms for the system. The objection undermines the evidence route; it does not refute the thesis. It is answered if the operators' objectives are themselves produced and revised by the organization. | Proposed |
